lead.headline: U.S. aircraft disables merchant ship running the Iran blockade
lead.dek: Central Command says it fired on the stern of the Palau-flagged Pacific Archer in the Gulf of Oman after warnings; the crew was unharmed
body: The U.S. military disabled a merchant ship in the Gulf of Oman that was trying to run its blockade of Iranian ports, U.S. Central Command said Friday. A military aircraft fired precision munitions at the stern of the Palau-flagged M/V Pacific Archer on Thursday after the crew was given multiple warnings, the command said.

The ship's propulsion was disabled and its civilian crew was unharmed, Central Command said. The vessel had left the Iranian port of Bandar Abbas, and ship-tracking sites listed its destination as Singapore. Since the blockade resumed in July, the military says it has redirected 158 compliant ships and disabled six that refused, the last on Nov. 7.

The strike comes as the administration weighs its options in the war with Iran, which began in late February and has settled into a stalemate; Trump said Friday the war will end whenever he wants. Iran's navy commander, Shahram Irani, said on state television Friday that Iran will carry out operations to break the blockade. The Pacific Archer is at least the 15th vessel disabled since spring.

briefs.headline: Mexico files formal complaint over DEA cartel tip line
briefs.summary: President Claudia Sheinbaum said Friday Mexico lodged a complaint with U.S. Ambassador Ron Johnson after the DEA opened anonymous tip lines in Sinaloa, calling the move interference.

briefs.headline: U.S. official confirms hackers breached Air Force cloud platform
briefs.summary: A U.S. official told NBC News on Friday that intruders penetrated Cloud One, the Air Force's flagship cloud system, confirming a Reuters report; the Pentagon said its systems are secure.

briefs.headline: Thousands protest electric rates and cost of living in San Juan
briefs.summary: Some 30 unions, student and religious groups led a Black Friday 'Day of National Outrage' outside the Caribbean's largest mall over record electric rates and failing services, the AP reported.

briefs.headline: Two American Airlines jets clip wings while taxiing at Reagan National
briefs.summary: Flight 638 to Dallas struck the wingtip of Flight 2152 to Chicago shortly after 5 p.m. Friday while both taxied for departure, the FAA said. No one was hurt; both planes were pulled for inspection.

briefs.headline: MSF says Israeli strike on Gaza City clinic kills two staff
briefs.summary: Doctors Without Borders said two watchmen died Friday night in a direct hit on a marked clinic whose location the Israeli military knew; the military said the two were Hamas members. MSF puts its Gaza staff toll at 17.

briefs.headline: Taiwan counts local election votes with New Taipei on a knife edge
briefs.summary: Polls closed at 4 p.m. Saturday across 22 cities and counties; by 6:43 p.m. KMT incumbents led Taipei and Taoyuan, the DPP led Taichung, Tainan and Kaohsiung, and New Taipei sat near 50-50, CNA's live count showed.

briefs.headline: Kenyan court convicts cult leader over 123 starvation deaths
briefs.summary: A Mombasa court on Friday found Paul Mackenzie and 29 followers, including his wife, guilty of manslaughter for urging members to fast to death; he is already serving 200 years for the murders of 191 people.

briefs.headline: UN's Albanese leaves Costa Rica airport after court order
briefs.summary: Francesca Albanese left San Jose's airport Saturday after two nights in transit; Costa Rica's Constitutional Chamber had ordered her moved to a hotel late Friday, and she said she would travel on to Mexico.

briefs.headline: State police arrest Bunker Hill man in Jefferson County triple murder
briefs.summary: Troopers arrested Alex Fuston, 26, without incident late Thursday at a Bunker Hill home in the Monday shooting deaths of three people in Kearneysville, state police said. He is held without bail.

briefs.headline: Legislature's website stays dark a week after cyber incident
briefs.summary: The Legislature's website, including the online state code, remained down Friday after a Nov. 19 cybersecurity incident, House spokeswoman Ann Ali said; interim meetings begin Dec. 5.

briefs.headline: Sierra Club flags Mason County data center as top polluter
briefs.summary: A Sierra Club report says Nscale's Monarch campus near Point Pleasant could emit 11 million tons of CO2 a year; state energy director Nicholas Preservati said the figures are permit maximums, not operations.

briefs.headline: Insurer warns 55,000 West Virginians could lose Medicaid
briefs.summary: Highmark Health Options president Jason Landers said Friday about 55,000 expanded-Medicaid adults risk losing coverage when 80-hour monthly work documentation starts Jan. 1.

regional.item: Some Milton customers still had no water or brown water Friday night after Thursday's main break, with a boil advisory to follow restoration.
Wheels that came off a tractor-trailer struck two vehicles on U.S. 19 at Summersville Friday morning; no one was hurt, the fire department said.

away.item: The Bennington Select Board on Monday ratified a five-year public works union contract with a 4.8% raise in fiscal 2028, the Banner reported.

hotspots.item: A Webster County Girl Scout received the national Girl Scout Medal of Honor Nov. 21 in Webster Springs for saving a choking friend on July 4, the Echo said.
North Topsail Beach rescinded its Thanksgiving state of emergency at 5 p.m. Friday after the nor'easter, but all town beach accesses remain closed, WWAY reported.

briefs.headline: Big Brothers Big Sisters pauses Prince George mentoring, lays off staff
briefs.summary: The nonprofit said Friday a cash shortfall forced it to halt its in-school and Connect group mentoring and lay off office and mentoring staff; its early learning centre and after-school care stay open.

briefs.headline: B.C. charge rate of 843 per 100,000 draws Prince George council concern
briefs.summary: Figures given to city officials show B.C. approved 843 criminal charges per 100,000 people last year, down from 1,040 in 2021, against 2,018 in Alberta and 4,368 in Saskatchewan, CKPG reported Friday.

briefs.headline: Former B.C. environment minister George Heyman dies at 77
briefs.summary: Heyman, Vancouver-Fairview MLA from 2013 and environment minister from 2017 to 2024, died Friday of cancer, former colleague Rob Fleming said. He led the BCGEU for three terms and built CleanBC.

briefs.headline: Police watchdog probes fatal RCMP shooting at Richmond mall
briefs.summary: Richmond RCMP said officers arresting a suspect at a business on No. 3 Road across from Yaohan Centre fired shots Friday afternoon and the man died; the Independent Investigations Office is investigating.

briefs.headline: Supreme Court upholds Quebec's Bill 21 in split ruling
briefs.summary: Six of seven justices found Friday that Quebec validly invoked the notwithstanding clause for its 2019 secularism law; the court split 4-3 on its validity and carved out members of the National Assembly.

briefs.headline: Carney names Mackenzie Valley Highway a project of national interest
briefs.summary: In Yellowknife Friday, Carney designated the 800-km all-season road from Wrigley to the Dempster Highway near Inuvik, costed at C$4.2 billion with C$3.1 billion in Budget 2026; work could start in late 2027.

briefs.headline: Draining peatlands caused 2.7% of human-driven warming, study finds
briefs.summary: An MIT-led model published Wednesday in Nature traces CO2 and methane from bogs drained since 1800; Europe supplied over half the CO2, and the effect nearly doubles by 2100 if water levels hold.

briefs.headline: Rocket Lab sets annual record with Thanksgiving launch
briefs.summary: An Electron lifted a Synspective radar satellite from New Zealand Thursday at 7 p.m. ET, the company's 22nd launch of 2026 and 101st overall by its own count; the craft was released at 569 km.

briefs.headline: Astronomers watch red giant swallow companion star in Andromeda
briefs.summary: A red giant of seven solar masses engulfed a smaller star, which spiraled into its core in under 10 orbits before an October 2025 eruption, a Columbia-led team reported Friday.

briefs.headline: Utah trial sends first sensory bionic hand home with a patient
briefs.summary: A University of Utah clinical trial has let its ninth implant recipient take a nerve-wired LUKE arm home, the first to use the pressure-sensing hand on his own outside the lab, the magazine reported Thursday.

briefs.headline: OpenAI countersues Apple in trade-secrets fight
briefs.summary: OpenAI filed counterclaims Friday in federal court in California, alleging Apple's employment practices set a trap to accuse departing workers of theft. Apple called the filing a distraction.

briefs.headline: SAP plans to cut at least 10,000 jobs in AI restructuring
briefs.summary: SAP is preparing to eliminate at least 10,000 positions, about 9% of its 110,000 staff, as it reorganizes around AI, Bloomberg reported Friday, citing people familiar with the matter.

briefs.headline: Nature examines rumors that AI labs can break RSA encryption
briefs.summary: Nature reported Thursday on unconfirmed claims among researchers that OpenAI and Anthropic hold fast algorithms against RSA; the journal said it could not confirm them, and neither company has.

weather_ear: Saturday's forecast comes at 7:15, from Jim Claudtore.
kicker: Putnam-Kanawha, the Mid-Ohio Valley and Summers-New River carry no regional line today; the Hatsu basho opens Jan. 10 in Tokyo, 43 days out.
